---
title: "What Drives Home Prices?"
---



## Overview

This analysis identifies which home features have the strongest impact on sale prices using:
- **Correlation analysis** (Week 6)
- **Hypothesis testing** (Week 7)
- **ANOVA** (Week 8)

---

## Top Price Drivers (Correlation Analysis)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Calculate key correlations
correlations <- data.frame(
  Feature = c("Overall Quality", "Living Area", "Garage Area", 
              "Basement Area", "Year Built"),
  Correlation = c(
    cor(ames$Overall.Qual, ames$SalePrice),
    cor(ames$Gr.Liv.Area, ames$SalePrice),
    cor(ames$Garage.Area, ames$SalePrice, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(ames$Total.Bsmt.SF, ames$SalePrice, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(ames$Year.Built, ames$SalePrice)
  )
) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)))

kable(correlations, digits = 3,
      caption = "Top 5 Features Correlated with Sale Price")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


Table: Top 5 Features Correlated with Sale Price

|Feature         | Correlation|
|:---------------|-----------:|
|Overall Quality |       0.799|
|Living Area     |       0.707|
|Garage Area     |       0.640|
|Basement Area   |       0.632|
|Year Built      |       0.558|


:::
:::


**Key Finding:** Overall Quality (r = 0.80) and Living Area (r = 0.71) are the strongest predictors.

## Feature Impact: Hypothesis Tests

### Central Air Conditioning


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create the groups FIRST
ac_yes <- ames %>% filter(Central.Air == "Y") %>% pull(SalePrice)
ac_no <- ames %>% filter(Central.Air == "N") %>% pull(SalePrice)

# Then run the t-test
t_result <- t.test(ac_yes, ac_no)

cat("Homes WITH Central Air: mean =", dollar(mean(ac_yes)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Homes WITH Central Air: mean = $186,453 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Homes WITHOUT Central Air: mean =", dollar(mean(ac_no)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Homes WITHOUT Central Air: mean = $101,890 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Difference:", dollar(mean(ac_yes) - mean(ac_no)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Difference: $84,562.31 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("P-value:", format(t_result$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
P-value: 8.784936e-88 
```


:::
:::


**P-value interpretation:**

The p-value of 8.784936e-88 means:

- **If central air had NO effect** on price (null hypothesis true)
- The probability of observing a difference of $84,562 or more extreme
- **Is less than 0.001** (0.1%)

In other words: This result is so extreme that it's virtually impossible to have occurred by chance alone if AC truly didn't matter. We have **very strong evidence** that central air increases home values.

**Statistical significance:** ✓ p < 0.001 (highly significant)  
**Practical significance:** $84,562 difference is substantial (approximately 47% of median home price)

---

### Recent Construction (2000+)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create binary variable for recent construction
ames <- ames %>%
  mutate(Is_Recent = Year.Built >= 2000)

recent <- ames %>% filter(Is_Recent) %>% pull(SalePrice)
older <- ames %>% filter(!Is_Recent) %>% pull(SalePrice)

t_result2 <- t.test(recent, older, alternative = "greater")

cat("Recent homes (2000+): mean =", dollar(mean(recent)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Recent homes (2000+): mean = $248,521 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Older homes (<2000): mean =", dollar(mean(older)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Older homes (<2000): mean = $156,097 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Difference:", dollar(mean(recent) - mean(older)), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Difference: $92,424.14 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("P-value:", format(t_result2$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
P-value: 1.438068e-126 
```


:::
:::


**P-value interpretation:**

The p-value of 1.438068e-126 means:

- **If construction year had NO effect** on price (null hypothesis true)
- The probability of observing a difference of $92,424 or more extreme
- **Is less than 0.001** (0.1%)

**Finding:** Recently built homes (2000+) sell for **$92,424** more on average than older homes.

**Statistical significance:** ✓ p < 0.001 (highly significant)  
**Practical significance:** This $92K+ premium represents a 51% increase over the average older home price

---

## House Style Effect (ANOVA)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ANOVA test
anova_result <- aov(SalePrice ~ House.Style, data = ames)
anova_summary <- summary(anova_result)

cat("ANOVA F-statistic:", round(anova_summary[[1]]["House.Style", "F value"], 2), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
ANOVA F-statistic: 35.04 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("P-value:", format(anova_summary[[1]]["House.Style", "Pr(>F)"], scientific = TRUE), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
P-value: 3.02871e-47 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("\n✓ House style DOES affect price (p < 0.001)\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

✓ House style DOES affect price (p < 0.001)
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Mean price by style
style_summary <- ames %>%
  group_by(House.Style) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),
    Mean_Price = mean(SalePrice),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean_Price))

kable(style_summary, 
      col.names = c("House Style", "Count", "Mean Price"),
      digits = 0)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|House Style | Count| Mean Price|
|:-----------|-----:|----------:|
|2.5Fin      |     8|     220000|
|2Story      |   873|     206990|
|1Story      |  1481|     178700|
|2.5Unf      |    24|     177158|
|SLvl        |   128|     165527|
|SFoyer      |    83|     143473|
|1.5Fin      |   314|     137530|
|1.5Unf      |    19|     109663|


:::
:::


**P-value interpretation:**

The p-value < 0.001 from the ANOVA test means:

- **If house style had NO effect** on price (all styles have same mean price)
- The probability of observing differences this large between groups
- **Is less than 0.1%**

**Finding:** Two-story homes command highest prices (mean: ~$200K), while split-level/multi-level homes have lowest prices (mean: ~$140K).

**Statistical significance:** ✓ p < 0.001 (highly significant)  
**Practical significance:** $60K+ difference between highest and lowest style types

---

## Summary: Price Driver Rankings

**Top 5 drivers (by effect size):**

1. **Overall Quality** (r = 0.80) - Strongest predictor
2. **Living Area** (r = 0.71) - Size matters
3. **Recent Construction** (+$92K) - Buyers pay premium for new
4. **Central Air** (+$85K) - Modern necessity
5. **Garage Area** (r = 0.64) - Storage/parking valued

**Actionable insight:** Focus on quality improvements over size additions for best ROI.
